tldr: For the marginal causal dose curve and the full nondecreasing cone, this note proves a rough-regime phase diagram on its bespoke derivativewise mixed H\"older benchmark. For each fixed public \(0<\beta\le1/6\), the original-record separation has exact order \(n^{-4\beta/(1+4\beta)}\), attained by a total finite multiresolution test with finite-sample full-null errors and matched by a normalized original Bernoulli mixture against every randomized test. Supplying the actual entire assignment density on the identical family gives upper \(32n^{-2/5}\) and explicit lower \(2^{-66}n^{-2/5}\exp(-5\sqrt{\log n})\) above \(2^{4096}\). The lower follows by optimizing the existing moment-matching degree with uniform exponential constants. For \(\beta>1/6\), the original radius has the same explicit lower and a \(C_{1/6}n^{-2/5}\) upper; the information ratio lies between one and \(2^{66}C_{1/6}\exp(5\sqrt{\log n})\). The rough price exponent and the retained \(\beta=1/10\) rate \(n^{-2/7}\) with price \(n^{4/35+o(1)}\) are unchanged. Exact supplied-density logarithms and smooth-phase constant-factor saturation remain unresolved.
